newsitem.title: USA: FBI interest in Jewell may be waning - paper.
newsitem.headline: FBI interest in Jewell may be waning - paper.

text.p: The FBI's interest in Richard Jewell, the only named suspect in this summer's Centennial Olympic Park bombing, appears to be waning, the Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported on Tuesday.

Jewell's criminal lawyer, Jack Martin, told the newspaper federal investigators have scaled back surveillance of the former security guard and are about to release most of the property seized from him during a series of searches.
Jewell was a security guard at the Olympic Park when a bomb exploded July 27 during a free concert in downtown Atlanta, leaving two dead and wounding more than 100 people.
FBI officials in Atlanta were not immediately available to comment on the report.

Until recently, FBI agents maintained round-the-clock surveillance outside the apartment the 33-year-old man shares with his mother, and three to six cars would follow Jewell wherever he went, according to the newspaper.
"Now, there appears to be no surveillance, unless it is absolutely covert and totally unobtrusive," said Martin.
"Every day, they seem to be less and less interested in Richard being a viable suspect."

Martin also told the Journal-Constitution the FBI was returning "most of the property" seized from Jewell during searches of his suburban Atlanta apartment, a rural cabin where he once lived and a shed in north Georgia.

Jewell initially was hailed as a hero after the bombing. A security guard at an AT&T pavillion, he had discovered a green knapsack containing a pipebomb, alerted police and helped move concert-goers from the area.
But within days, unnamed federal sources told the press that Jewell had become a suspect in the investigation.
Jewell, who has never been charged with any crime, steadfastly maintains his innocence and recently said he could sue the FBI and members of the media for ruining his chances for employment.
Last week, he set up his own telephone hotline for public donations to help make ends meet and to pay legal fees from his four-member team of attorneys.
